entries.english:
A huge, glowing, four-limbed purple creature with heightened senses, created by
the Orb itself. It guards the Orb with enormous punctiliousness and violence,
and its death will alert any Boundless Tesseracts on the level to begin creating
reinforcements.

Unless the Orb has already been disturbed, it will refuse to abandon its duty
by leaving the floor.
entries.translation:
一个巨大、发光、拥有四肢的紫色生物，感官敏锐，由宝珠本身创造。它以极端严谨和暴力守卫宝珠；死亡会惊动本层所有无垠超立方体，使其开始制造援军。

除非宝珠已经被惊动，否则它绝不离开本层，放弃职责。

issues.expected: 地面/楼层/地板/向下取整

entries.english:
A globe of profound nothingness and the oblivion that awaits all things - flesh,
souls, and even time itself. When the universe ends, only these will remain.
entries.translation: 一个由深邃虚无，以及等待血肉、灵魂乃至时间本身的湮灭构成的球体。宇宙终结时，唯有它们仍将存在。

entries.english:
A servant of Beogh, the ancient god of the orcs. Beogh rewards its devoted
prayers by striking down its enemies.
entries.translation: 兽人古神比欧弗的仆从。比欧弗会击倒它的敌人，作为对虔诚祈祷的回应。

issues.review: context_review:普通击打或叩击，不是专名

entries.english:
An intricate mechanical beetle covered in reinforced metal plates that resemble
a shield. It projects a kinetic barrier around its creator while adjacent to
them, increasing their armour class.

It will never voluntarily leave its creator's side, and if forcibly seperated,
will prioritise returning to them over any other concerns.
entries.translation:
一只精巧的机械甲虫，覆盖着盾牌般的强化金属甲片。与创造者相邻时，它会在对方周围投射动能屏障，提高护甲值。

它永远不会主动离开创造者身旁；若被强行分开，会优先返回，顾不上其他事情。

entries.english:
A hideous translucent green spirit of a warrior fallen in battle but recalled
to this plane by unholy magic. The blade it wields is ethereal, rendering those
it strikes weak-willed and vulnerable to dark magic.
entries.translation:
一个可怕的、幽绿色的战败战士的灵魂，被邪恶魔法召回到这个层面。
它所持的利刃是虚无的，被它伤到的会更易受魔法影响。

entries.english:
An otherworldly spider that can move short and medium distances by briefly
shifting between the planes of reality, in order to better ensnare its prey.
entries.translation:
这只奇异的蜘蛛通过在多个现实位面中相位来快速进行中短距离移动，
以便更轻松地捕住它的猎物。

issues.review: context_review:诱捕、蛛网或束缚动作，不是法术名称

entries.english:
A leftover mess of broken bones, inert grasping organs, and scattered skin.
While some highly-specialised sorcerers might be capable of bringing it to life,
it is otherwise harmless - the possible leftovers of some departed or
absent-minded magus.
entries.translation: 一堆剩下的碎骨、已不活动的抓握器官与散落皮肤。除非由某些专精此道的术士赋予生命，否则完全无害，或许是某位离去或心不在焉的法师留下的东西。

entries.english:
A gleaming warrior, wrought from precious metals and the very pinnacle of
forgecraft techniques. Its every motion flows with a deadly, fluid grace that
belies its artifical nature.
entries.translation: 一位闪亮的战士，由贵金属与锻造术的巅峰技艺铸成。每个动作都流露出致命而流畅的优雅，令人难以相信它是人造之物。

entries.english:
The apparition of an unfortunate adventurer, retaining many of the skills and
abilities the adventurer had in life. It is condemned to haunt this particular
level of the dungeons, lashing out violently at the next adventurer to cross
its path.
entries.translation:
这是某个不幸冒险者的鬼魂，它依然保有着许多生前拥有的技能和能力。
它被诅咒，徘徊在这一层地牢，向碰见它的下一个冒险者发起猛烈的攻击。

issues.review: context_review:徘徊、作祟的动作，不是鬼魂缠身法术

entries.english:
Many poltergeists are fiercely territorial over the domains they choose to
haunt, but these have extended that protection even to the people who share
their domain with them. Some say they must be the lingering souls of those who
guarded the Vaults in life; others suggest the Ironbound Order simply recruited
them in common cause. Whichever is true, their very presence shelters other
creatures from missiles, causing sling and spell alike to veer off-course at the
last moment.
entries.translation: 许多骚灵会凶猛捍卫自己选择作祟的领地，而这些骚灵则把保护范围扩展到与自己共居的人。有的说，它们是生前守卫宝库者留下的灵魂；也有人说，铁缚会只是因共同目标将它们招募。不论真相如何，它们仅仅在场，就能保护其他生物免受飞弹侵袭，使投石和法术都在最后一刻偏离方向。

issues.review: context_review:徘徊、作祟的动作，不是鬼魂缠身法术

entries.english:
A starved spirit whose mouth is a pit of rot, emitting vile fumes. Its putrid
maw cannot eat the food it finds, so it moans with rage and desparate hunger.
entries.translation:
一个饥饿的灵魂，它的嘴是个腐烂的坑，散发着恶臭。
它那腐烂的嘴无法吃它找到的食物，愤怒地呻吟着，绝望地饿着。

entries.english:
A long and sinuous dragon, seemingly more neck and tail than anything else. Its
skin shines like molten mercury, magical energies arc from its pointed snout,
and it moves with terrifying swiftness.
entries.translation:
一条长而蜷曲着的龙，看起来几乎完全是颈和尾巴。
它的皮肤像熔铸的水银一样发着光，口鼻喷射着魔法能量，而且它的动作迅捷得吓人。

issues.review: context_review:普通速度描述或迅捷效果，保留上下文表达

entries.english:
A giant cockroach that has been exposed to high amounts of mutagenic energy. It
is horrifyingly mutated, but this has only made it stronger.
entries.translation:
一个暴露于大量诱变能量的巨型蟑螂。
它发生了可怕的变异，但这只会让它变得更强大。

entries.english:
A timeworn revenant whose flames dance with the silhouettes of long-forgotten
atrocities. Cursed with a hunger they can never satisfy, they unleash these
long-dead echoes to reenact violence upon any soul they deem worthy of adding to
their eternal collection.
entries.translation: 一个久经岁月的还魂者，火焰中跃动着早被遗忘的暴行剪影。它受永远无法满足的饥渴诅咒，释放这些久已死去的回响，再演昔日暴力，将自认值得收藏的灵魂添入永恒藏品。

issues.review: context_review:渴望、饥渴描述，不是饥饿值

entries.english:
A mountain hobgoblin, recently come in search of the legendary Orb. Not
foolhardy or reckless enough to delve into the depths of the Dungeon alone,
Robin has built a small army of minions. Potential competitors will quickly
find a stream of screaming goblins flying toward them!
entries.translation: 一位山地大地精，最近来到地下城寻找传说中的宝珠。罗宾还没鲁莽到独自深入地下城，而是集结了一小支随从军队。潜在竞争者很快就会发现，一串尖叫着的地精正朝自己飞来！

issues.review: context_review:普通深处描述，不是深处以外的分支名
context_review:普通深处描述，不是分支名称

entries.english:
Rippling muscles, glistening pecs, incredible glutes - Rupert is the peak of
physical perfection. Even so, his roars seem louder than even his fantastic form
can explain. Perhaps he holds some talisman that lends supernatural force to his
bellows?
entries.translation:
起伏的肌肉、闪亮的胸肌、巨大的臀肌——鲁珀特达到了完美肉体的巅峰。
即便如此，他的咆哮似乎比以他那种奇异体形所能吼出的还要响亮。
也许，正是他持有的某个符咒，给他的吼叫带来了超自然的力量？

issues.review: context_review:普通符咒，不是变形护符装备

entries.english:
A red, flaming half-human half-snake creature with a legendary affinity for
fire.
entries.translation: 一个红色的、燃烧的半人半蛇的生物，传说和火的关系很密切。

issues.review: context_review:人、半人或可读性语境，允许中文省略类字

entries.english:
A small, human-shaped agglomeration of salt. It was created by the last
fugitive loyalists of the fallen eastern empire, forced in desperation to
construct golems from local resources to defend themselves.
entries.translation:
一个小型的人形盐块。它是由最后一批忠于没落的东方帝国的逃亡者创建的，
他们在绝望中被迫用当地资源建造魔像来保护自己。

entries.english:
Seemingly three pairs of lurid magenta eyes hanging in the darkness, the
outline of a vast, sinuous dragon is just barely perceptible behind. Its malice
is palpable.
entries.translation:
黑暗中似乎悬着三双可怕的洋红色眼睛，后面一条蜿蜒的巨龙轮廓隐约可见。
其恶意昭然若揭。

entries.english:
A member of an order of monks who abandoned their former faith. It now serves
a minor god of wind and whispers, who allows it to calm the air and, when
in great need, to break the stillness with divine thunder.
entries.translation:
一个放弃原先信仰的僧侣。
现在他侍奉掌管风和低语的低阶的神，这使得他能让空气平静下来，
或是非常需要的时候，用神圣的雷声打破寂静。

issues.review: context_review:低阶恶魔、亚龙等语境，不是次级法术前缀

entries.english:
A mysterious demonic figure, difficult to distinguish from the darkness around
it. It weaves the shadows into powerful minions.
entries.translation: 一个神秘的魔鬼，很难把它从周围的黑暗中分辨出来。它把阴影编成强大的仆从。

entries.english: A shadowy minor demon, with an affinity for the necromantic arts.
entries.translation: 一个影状低阶恶魔，擅长死灵技艺。

issues.review: context_review:低阶恶魔、亚龙等语境，不是次级法术前缀

entries.english:
A minor servant of living shadow whose form wavers perpetually on the edge of
recognition - as if an unseen light were flickering behind something almost
familiar.

The strength of its attacks increases in proportion with the power of the spell
which summoned it.
entries.translation:
一个活体阴影构成的小仆从，其形态永远徘徊在似曾相识的边缘，仿佛某种看不见的光，正从几乎熟悉的事物后闪烁。

其攻击强度与召来它的法术强度成正比。

entries.english:
A strangely static silhouette whose form suggests a large cannon. Though it uses
no gunpowder, the depths of its bore flickers angrily with every shot, as if
remembering the fiery light of its ignition.
entries.translation: 一个奇异静止的剪影，外形像一门大炮。虽然不用火药，每次射击时，炮膛深处仍会愤怒闪动，仿佛记得点火时的烈光。

issues.review: context_review:火炮点火，不是法术名称

entries.english:
A skulking apparition that disguises itself as a harmless shadow. Attuned to the
dim light of the dungeon, it can slip in and out of sight at will, moving
swiftly from one pool of shade to the next before striking unerringly at the
blind spots of those who cannot see it.
entries.translation: 一个潜行的幽魂，伪装成无害影子。它适应地下城昏暗的光线，能随意显隐，迅速从一片阴影移向另一片，然后精准袭击看不见它的目标的盲点。

issues.review: context_review:普通击打或叩击，不是专名

entries.english:
An incredibly fast-moving bird, known for impaling its prey on shards of ice
before tearing them to pieces. It has acclimated to the desolate wastes of
Cocytus, and is enveloped with an accursed chill.
entries.translation:
一个移动速度极快的⻦，因为会在撕碎猎物前用冰碎片将其刺穿而闻名。
它已适应悲叹河那荒凉的废墟，被严酷的寒意裹挟着。

issues.review: context_review:严酷寒意的修辞，非状态标签

entries.english:
A terrible spirit which brings an unearthly silence to the area around it,
making it impossible to recite the magical incantations involved with casting
spells or reading scrolls.
entries.translation:
这个可怕的幽魂给周围区域带来超乎寻常的寂静，
身处结界中的时候无法吟诵魔法咒语，也就不能施放魔法或是阅读卷轴。

issues.review: context_review:吟诵或诵读动作，不强制套用能力标题

entries.english:
A small vile creature that moves in bursts, stopping then darting with
lightning speed. It sprays sparks as it goes.
entries.translation: 这个邪恶的小东西会突然停下，然后又以闪电般的速度突进。它边走边迸出电火花。

entries.english: A skeleton compelled to unlife by the exercise of necromancy.
entries.translation: 一具被死灵法术复活的骷髅。

entries.english:
Skysharks cut through the air with a thoughtless ease. Just a taste of blood
gives them an enraged strength, and further morsels drive them into a frenzy.
entries.translation:
天鲨自在地划过天空。
哪怕只有一丝血也能激起它们愤怒的力量，要是有更多的鲜血会使其陷入疯狂。

issues.review: context_review:疯狂或狂暴描述，按具体效果表述

entries.english:
A surprisingly ambulatory mushroom. It wafts its spores over prey to send them
into a deep sleep, making it simple for the fungus to kill and devour them.
It can take months for its mycelia to fully infiltrate and digest victims.
entries.translation:
一个令人惊奇的会走动的蘑菇。它能将孢子飘散到猎物身上，
使猎物进入深度睡眠，这样真菌就能轻易杀死并吞噬它们。
菌丝可能需要数月时间才能完全侵入并消化受害者。

entries.english:
A swift and sinuous vine brought alive by a dryad's magic. It can quickly bind
and entangle the dryad's foes, dragging them back to the forest from which it
surges.
entries.translation:
一个迅捷而蜿蜒的藤蔓，被德律阿得斯用魔法赋予生命。
它能快速将德律阿得斯的敌人束缚、缠绕住，将他们拖回它所涌现的森林。

entries.english:
Part of a swift and sinuous vine brought alive by a dryad's magic. It can
quickly bind and entangle the dryad's foes, dragging them back to the forest
from which it surges.
entries.translation:
一节迅捷而蜿蜒的藤蔓，被德律阿得斯用魔法赋予生命。
它能快速将德律阿得斯的敌人束缚、缠绕住，将他们拖回它所涌现的森林。

entries.english:
Queen of the tengu, with legendary skill in swordsmanship, tactics, and magic.
Storytellers claim she once trapped a raging tempest in a bottle and kept it
as a talisman.
entries.translation:
天狗女王，其剑术、谋略和魔法出神入化。
讲故事的人说，她曾把一场强烈的风暴捕获在一个瓶子里，并把它当作符咒保存着。

issues.review: context_review:训练目标、本领、技艺等完整中文表达
context_review:普通符咒，不是变形护符装备

entries.english:
An elite, well-equipped spriggan warrior, renowned for its unbelievable agility
and its prowess with advanced weaponry.
entries.translation:
一名装备精良的斯普利根战士，
他靠他精湛的武器技能和难以置信的灵巧赢得了同胞的尊敬。

entries.english:
A large worm covered with hard, spiky metal plates. Despite the apparent
heaviness of its outer armour, it is rather fast.
entries.translation: 一条覆有硬而多刺的金属板的大蠕虫。尽管它的外甲看起来很重，但速度相当快。

entries.english: <acid blob>
entries.translation: <acid blob>

entries.english:
A small and slimy dragon, covered in swamp muck and giving off a terrible
stench.
entries.translation: 这条小龙浑身上下都是黏液和污泥，散发着可怕的恶臭。

issues.review: context_review:沼气或沼泽污泥，不是沼泽分支

entries.english:
Before even the oldest of ancient liches mastered life and death, a group of
titans attempted to pull themselves free of mortality through brute strength.
They almost succeeded before rot dragged them to Ereshkigal. A glimmer of their
former beauty remains, alluring despite the stench.
entries.translation:
在最早的远古巫妖掌握生死之前，就曾有一群泰坦试图通过蛮力摆脱死亡。
在腐烂将他们拖到埃列什基伽勒那里之前，他们几乎要成功了。
尽管留有恶臭，但仍保留着他们昔日美丽的微光。

issues.review: context_review:强度、蛮力或威力，不是力量属性标签

entries.english: Those who enter will not escape.
entries.translation: 进入的人无法再逃脱。

entries.english: His shield is emblazoned with images of infernal flames.
entries.translation: 他的盾上饰有地狱火的图案。

entries.english:
You hear the echoes of planets behind the deafening roar of stars as it
approaches. It is the jaws of the abyss. It brings forth crawling chaos from
within. It is the last sight you will ever see.
entries.translation: 它靠近时，你在恒星震耳欲聋的咆哮之后，听到行星的回声。它是深渊的巨颚，从内部释放蠕行的混沌。这将是你此生最后看到的景象。

entries.english:
The earthly avatar of Tiamat, deity of dragonkind, here incarnated as a mighty
draconian warrior. Her scales seem to shimmer and change colour as you watch.
entries.translation:
提亚玛特的现世化身，龙族的神，在这里具现为强大的龙人战士。
当你观察她时，她的鳞片似乎会闪耀并变幻颜色。

entries.english:
A short-lived species of fungus typically found on or around decaying organic
matter.
entries.translation: 这个短命的真菌通常只在腐烂的有机物附近出现。

entries.english:
A malign devil covered in all manner of claws, spines, and cruel hooks. It is
able to inflict torturous agony on those foolish enough to gaze upon it.
entries.translation:
这个凶悍的恶魔身上全是爪子、骨刺、倒钩之类的东西。
它能让蠢到敢于直视它的人体验极端的痛苦。

entries.english:
A ponderous gastropod with a rock-hard shell. It is said to be in some way
connected with the god Cheibriados; its very presence slows the movements of
unwary adventurers, leaving them easy prey for its terrifying, ever-gnashing
radulae.
entries.translation: 一种行动迟缓、壳硬如岩石的腹足动物。据说与切布理亚多有某种联系；它仅仅在场，就会减缓冒失冒险者的行动，让他们轻易成为骇人、不断啃咬的齿舌下的猎物。

issues.review: context_review:神名、代词或 Lua 标识符覆盖含义

entries.english:
A huge and physically powerful humanoid creature. Short on intelligence but
long on brawn, its thick knobbly hide heals rapidly from most wounds.
entries.translation:
一个体形巨大、身体强壮的人形生物。
他头脑简单，但肌肉发达，而且他那结节状的厚皮能迅速愈合大多数伤口。

issues.review: context_review:智慧、头脑、心智描述，不强制用智力属性名

entries.english: A whirling vortex of frost.
entries.translation: 一个冰霜旋涡。

issues.review: context_review:涡旋或旋涡的物理描述，不是完整法术名

entries.english:
A colossal mass of bones and skulls, a walking tomb. You hear shrieks and
screams as it approaches, shattering off bones with each crushing step,
reassembling itself in eternal unrest.
entries.translation:
大堆骨头和头骨，它简直是个行走的坟墓。当它接近时，你会听到尖叫和呼啸，
每个步伐都是毁灭性的，骨头在碎裂，同时又无休止地进行重组。

entries.english:
A chattering and shrieking minor demon. They delight in sneaking past and
backstabbing their prey.
entries.translation: 这个低阶恶魔总爱发出啁啾声和尖啸声。他们喜欢溜过猎物，然后对其发动背刺。

issues.review: context_review:低阶恶魔、亚龙等语境，不是次级法术前缀

entries.english:
The Dungeon's vast repositories of the dead and the unholy realms thereafter
both require regular restocking and reorganisation, far beyond the coordination
of the restless dead. These corpse-collecting constructs burrow through the
earth and command divisions of zombified hands to assist them in stealing away
carrion, and may also violently create new corpses for such purposes.
entries.translation: 地下城庞大的亡者库藏，以及往后的邪恶领域，都需要定期补充与整理，这远非躁动死者能协调完成。这些收尸构造物在地下钻行，指挥成群丧尸之手协助偷运腐尸，也可能通过暴力制造新尸体来完成工作。

entries.english:
A swirling tempest of souls and steel: knights and blacksmiths and
weaponmasters, all bound to weapons they once held in life. To fight one is like
fighting an entire army.
entries.translation: 一场灵魂与钢铁的旋风：骑士、铁匠与武器大师，全都被束缚在生前持用的武器上。与其交战，就像对抗整支军队。

issues.review: context_review:普通作战或格斗语境，不是技能标签

entries.english:
A sorcerer who, by accident or design, has been afflicted with the curse of the
vampire. Regardless, through undeath, it has finally mastered the art of dark
magic.
entries.translation:
不管是自愿的还是被迫的，这名术士是受到了吸血的诅咒。
但不管怎么说，在不死之力的帮助下，这名法师终于完全掌握了黑暗魔法的奥秘。

entries.english:
A mosquito that has fed upon tainted blood and been transformed into a
revolting and pestilent undead insect, seeking to drain its victims to the last
drop.
entries.translation:
这只蚊子以受污染的血液为食，变成了一只令人作呕、散播疾病的亡灵昆虫。
它的目的是将它的猎物吸干——一滴不留。

issues.review: context_review:消耗魔力、吸干鲜血等语境，不是吸能状态

entries.english:
A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic,
forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically
erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells.

It is encrusted with long, sharp, deadly-looking crystals.
entries.translation:
一本很久没有读过的魔法书。它充满魔力，它的封皮形成了厚厚的盔甲，
书页长出了腿，并周期性地爆出自由飘浮的自行施放的法术。

它镶嵌着长而锋利的致命水晶。

entries.english:
A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic,
forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically
erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells.

Its cover bears the icon of a long-forgotten god, still fully possessed of wrath.
entries.translation:
一本很久没有读过的魔法书。它充满魔力，它的封皮形成了厚厚的盔甲，
书页长出了腿，并周期性地爆出自由飘浮的自行施放的法术。

它的封面上有一个被遗忘已久的神像，仍然充满着愤怒。

entries.english:
A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic,
forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically
erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells.

It is coated with impossibly ancient dust.
entries.translation:
一本很久没有读过的魔法书。它充满魔力，它的封皮形成了厚厚的盔甲，
书页长出了腿，并周期性地爆出自由飘浮的自行施放的法术。

它被一层不可思议的古老灰尘覆盖着。

entries.english:
A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic,
forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically
erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells.

It glistens with a thick layer of unmelting ice.
entries.translation:
一本很久没有读过的魔法书。它充满魔力，它的封皮形成了厚厚的盔甲，
书页长出了腿，并周期性地爆出自由飘浮的自行施放的法术。

它那层未融化的坚冰在闪烁着。

entries.english:
A spellbook that has gone too long without being read. It overflows with magic,
forming thick armour from its binding, legs from its pages, and periodically
erupting in flurries of free-floating, self-casting spells.
entries.translation:
一本很久没有读过的魔法书。它充满魔力，它的封皮形成了厚厚的盔甲，
书页长出了腿，并周期性地爆出自由飘浮的自行施放的法术。

entries.english:
A smooth statue of a beautiful merfolk bathing in a fountain, sculpted from
creamy, faintly pinkish travertine. It glistens softly in the light.
entries.translation:
一尊光滑的在泉中沐浴的人鱼雕像，由奶油色、略带浅粉色的钙华雕刻而成。
它在光线下中柔和地闪耀着。

entries.english: A small and mischievous minor demon covered in frost.
entries.translation: 一个小而调皮的低阶恶魔，浑身都是冰霜。

entries.english:
An ancient warrior, kept in a state of perpetual undeath by its desire to die
with honour in battle.
entries.translation: 一位古代战士，怀着在战斗中光荣地死去的执念而永远保持着不死状态。

entries.english:
A green-glowing gaseous entity, flickering and pulsing irregularly as it hovers
through the air. Travelers have been known to confuse these for distant lanterns -
a mistake rarely made twice.
entries.translation:
一个绿色发光的气态实体，悬在空中，时时不规则地闪烁、悸动。
众所周知，旅行者会将这些与远方的灯笼相混淆——这种错误很少有机会犯两次。

issues.review: context_review:混淆对象的动作，不是混乱效果

entries.english:
An old and unnaturally ugly human, wearing robes stained with what appears to
be swamp ooze, cauldron soot and brew ingredients.
entries.translation: 一个年老而异常丑陋的人，所穿的长袍上沾染着沼泽淤泥、大锅的烟灰和酿造原料。

issues.review: context_review:人、半人或可读性语境，允许中文省略类字

entries.english:
A plant whose life has been drained away, but with its physical form still
intact. It looks like it died many {{ if you.branch() == "Crypt" or
you.branch() == "Tomb" or you.branch() == "Zot" then return "centuries";
else return "years"; end }} ago.

A small and strangely serpentine fold in space and time. Scholars once
theorised the Dungeon's easy access to manifold unholy realms is due to the
tunneling of yet-undiscovered translocations dragons. Whether or not this is
true, distant stars mottle this drake's endless lengths, and dimensions bend to
its writhing whim.
entries.translation: 时空中一道小巧、奇异蛇形的褶皱。学者曾推测，地下城之所以能方便地通往许多邪恶领域，是因为尚未发现的位移巨龙在那里掘洞。不论真相如何，遥远星辰斑驳地映在这条龙无尽的身躯上，维度也随它扭动的心意弯折。

entries.english:
A hybrid with the torso of a robust human atop the body of a yak. It excels in
ranged combat, and is also a formidable foe in close quarters.
entries.translation:
一个混种生物，在牦牛的身体上有着人的躯干。
他不但擅长远程战斗，近战方面也是个强大的敌人。

issues.review: context_review:健壮躯干的描述，不是强健变异名

entries.english:
A winged demon covered in shiny metallic scales. It has a legion of minor
demons under its command.
entries.translation: 一个有翼的恶魔，身上覆有闪耀的金属鳞片。它指挥着一个低阶恶魔军团。

issues.review: context_review:低阶恶魔、亚龙等语境，不是次级法术前缀

entries.translation: 成功施法时，你有一定几率收回消耗的魔力；施法失败时，则总能收回消耗的魔力。

You have a chance of causing visible monsters to go into a frenzy when you kill
a foe.
entries.translation: 你击杀敌人时有一定几率让视野内的怪物陷入狂乱。

entries.english:
“When Peleus, some distance away, saw him torn apart by the frightful wound he
 shouted: ‘Accept this tribute to the dead, at least, Crantor, dearest of
 youths’, and with his powerful arm, he hurled his ash spear, at full strength,
 at Demoleon. It ruptured the ribcage, and stuck quivering in the bone. The
 centaur pulled out the shaft minus its head (he tried with difficulty to reach
 that also) but the head was caught in his lung. The pain itself strengthened
 his will: wounded, he reared up at his enemy and beat the hero down with his
 hooves. Peleus received the resounding blows on helmet and shield, and
 defending his upper arms, and controlling the weapon he held out, with one
 blow through the arm he pierced the bi-formed breast.”
    -Ovid, _Metamorphoses_, XII, 330. 8 AD.
entries.translation:
“佩琉斯从远处看见他被可怕伤口撕裂，喊道：亲爱的克兰托尔，年轻人中最亲爱的，至少接受这份祭死贡礼。他奋力把白蜡木矛掷向德摩勒翁，刺裂肋笼，颤抖着钉入骨中。半人马拔出矛杆，却没拔出矛头，后者卡在肺里。痛苦反而增强斗志，他负伤立起，以蹄击倒英雄。佩琉斯用盔盾接住轰击，护住双臂，稳住武器，一击穿过对方手臂，刺入那双形的胸膛。”
    -Ovid, _Metamorphoses_, XII, 330. 8 AD.

entries.english:
“On the other hand, Confucius is made to say to his disciples, ‘I know how
 birds can fly, how fishes can swim, and how animals can run. But the runner
 may be snared, the swimmer may be hooked, and the flyer may be shot by the
 arrow. But there is the dragon. I cannot tell how he mounts on the wind
 through the clouds, and rises to heaven. Today I have seen Lao-tsze, and can
 only compare him to the dragon.’”
    -Life of Confucius

“This Dragon had Two furious Wings
   Each one upon each Shoulder;
 With a Sting in his Tail as long as a Flail,
   Which made him bolder and bolder.
 He had long Claws, and in his Jaws
   Four and forty Teeth of Iron;
 With a Hide as tough, as any Buff,
   Which did him round environ.”

    -“An Excellent Ballad of a most dreadful Combat, fought between Moore of
Moore-Hall, and the Dragon of Wantley”, retold by Ambrose Philips, _A
Collection of Old Ballads. Corrected from the Best and Most Ancient Copies
Extant. With Introductions Historical, Critical, Or Humorous_. 1723.
entries.translation:
孔子去，谓弟子曰：“鸟，吾知其能飞；鱼，吾知其能游；兽，吾知其能走。走者可以为罔，游者可以为纶，飞者可以为矰。至于龙，吾不能知其乘风云而上天。吾今日见老子，其犹龙邪！”
    -司马迁，《史记·老子韩非列传》

“这龙有两只凶猛翅膀，
一肩一只。
尾刺长得像连枷，
令它愈加大胆。
爪长，口中有
四十四颗铁牙，
坚韧如厚皮的外皮，
围护全身。”
    -“An Excellent Ballad of a most dreadful Combat, fought between Moore of
Moore-Hall, and the Dragon of Wantley”, retold by Ambrose Philips, _A
Collection of Old Ballads. Corrected from the Best and Most Ancient Copies
Extant. With Introductions Historical, Critical, Or Humorous_. 1723.

entries.english:
“The Parts Septentrionall are with these Sp'ryts Much haunted.. About the
 places where they dig for Oare. The Greekes and Germans call them Cobali.”
    -Thomas Heywood, _The Hierarchy of the Blessed Angels_, Book IX, l. 568.
1635.
entries.translation:
“北方地区常被这些精灵出没，尤其采矿之处。希腊人与德意志人称它们为 Cobali。”
    -Thomas Heywood, _The Hierarchy of the Blessed Angels_, Book IX, l. 568.
1635.

entries.english:
“The latter lived in the country, and before his house there was an oak, in
 which there was a lair of snakes. His servants killed the snakes, but Melampus
 gathered wood and burnt the reptiles, and reared the young ones. And when the
 young were full grown, they stood beside him at each of his shoulders as he
 slept, and they purged his ears with their tongues. He started up in a great
 fright, but understood the voices of the birds flying overhead, and from what
 he learned from them he foretold to men what should come to pass.”
    -Pseudo-Apollodorus , _Library and Epitome_, 1.9.11. circa 150 BC.
    trans. Sir James George Frazer, 1913.

“A snake, with mottles rare,
 Surveyed my chamber floor,
 In feature as the worm before,
 But ringed with power.”
    -Emily Dickinson, “In Winter In My Room”. circa 1860.
entries.translation:
“他住在乡间，屋前橡树中有蛇窝。仆人杀了蛇，墨兰波斯却捡柴焚葬蛇身，养育幼蛇。幼蛇长大后，在他睡眠时各守一肩，以舌舔净双耳。他惊醒，却能听懂头上飞鸟的声音，并据所闻向人预言未来。”
    -Pseudo-Apollodorus , _Library and Epitome_, 1.9.11. circa 150 BC.
    trans. Sir James George Frazer, 1913.

“一条斑纹罕见的蛇，
打量着我屋子的地板；
外貌似从前的蠕虫，
却环绕着力量。”
    -Emily Dickinson, “In Winter In My Room”. circa 1860.

entries.english:
“Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I
 perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and
 beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN
 GOD.”
    -KJV Bible, Acts 17:22-23.
entries.translation:
“保罗站在亚略巴古当中，说：雅典人哪，我看你们凡事很敬畏鬼神。我经过时，看见你们所敬拜的，甚至有一座坛，上面写着：献给未知之神。”
    -KJV Bible, Acts 17:22-23.

entries.english:
“I met a traveller from an antique land
 Who said: Two vast and trunkless legs of stone
 Stand in the desert. Near them on the sand,
 Half sunk, a shatter'd visage lies, whose frown
 And wrinkled lip and sneer of cold command
 Tell that its sculptor well those passions read
 Which yet survive, stamp'd on these lifeless things,
 The hand that mock'd them and the heart that fed.
 And on the pedestal these words appear:
 ‘My name is Ozymandias, king of kings:
 Look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair!’
 Nothing beside remains: round the decay
 Of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare,
 The lone and level sands stretch far away.”
    -Percy Bysshe Shelley, “Ozymandias”. 1818.
entries.translation:
“我遇见来自古老国度的旅人，
他说：两条没有躯干的巨大石腿
立在沙漠中。附近的沙上，
半埋着一张破碎面孔；紧锁的眉，
皱起的唇，冷酷发令的讥笑，
表明雕刻者深谙那些激情，
将其刻在无生命之物上，使它们
胜过摹刻的手与滋养它们的心而留存。
基座上刻着这些话：
‘我名奥西曼迪亚斯，万王之王：
强者啊，看我的功业，绝望吧！’
除此之外，一无所存。巨像残骸四周，
空旷而无边，孤寂平坦的沙漠
一直伸向远方。”
    -Percy Bysshe Shelley, “Ozymandias”. 1818.

entries.context: textdb:descript/quotes.txt:a one-way gate to the infinite horrors of the abyss
entries.english:
“And if you gaze for long into an abyss, the abyss gazes also into you.”
    -Friedrich Nietzsche, _Beyond Good and Evil_ , Aphorism 146. 1886.

“Well, in our country,” said Alice, still panting a little, “you'd generally
 get to somewhere else — if you ran very fast for a long time, as we've been
 doing.” “A slow sort of country!” said the Queen. “Now here, you see, it takes
 all the running you can do, to keep in the same place. If you want to get
 somewhere else, you must run at least twice as fast as that!”
    -Lewis Carroll, _Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There_,
ch. 2 “The Garden of Live Flowers”. 1871.
entries.translation:
“当你长久凝视深渊，深渊也在凝视你。”
    -Friedrich Nietzsche, _Beyond Good and Evil_ , Aphorism 146. 1886.

“可是在我们那儿，”爱丽丝仍微微喘着气说，“像我们这样跑得很快、跑上很久，通常就会到别的地方去。”
“多慢的国度！”王后说，“在这里，你得拼命跑，才能留在原地。想去别的地方，至少得跑得比这再快一倍！”
    -Lewis Carroll, _Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There_,
ch. 2 “The Garden of Live Flowers”. 1871.

entries.context: textdb:descript/quotes.txt:a portal to a secret trove of treasure
entries.english:
“He saw a large cavern and a vaulted [roof], in height equalling the stature
 of a full-grown man and it was hewn in the live stone and lighted up with
 light that came through air-holes and bullseyes in the upper surface of the
 rock which formed the roof. He had expected to find naught save outer gloom in
 this robbers' den, and he was surprised to see the whole room filled with
 bales of all manner stuffs, and heaped up from sole to ceiling with
 camel-loads of silks and brocades and embroidered cloths and mounds on mounds
 of vari-colored carpetings; besides which he espied coins golden and silvern
 without measure or account, some piled upon the ground and others bound in
 leathern bags and sacks. Seeing these goods and moneys in such abundance, Ali
 Baba determined in his mind that not during a few years only but for many
 generations thieves must have stored their gains and spoils in this place.”
    -_The Arabian Nights_. trans. Sir Richard F. Burton, 1885.
entries.translation:
“他看见一个大洞窟，拱顶约有成年人的身高，直接凿入岩石，光线从顶上岩面的通气孔和圆窗射入。他原以为盗窟只会一片漆黑，却惊见满屋各种货包，从地面到天花板堆满驼载的丝绸、锦缎、绣布，还有层层彩毯。他又看见数不清的金银钱币，有的堆在地上，有的装在皮袋中。面对如此丰富的货物与钱财，阿里巴巴断定，盗贼在此积存所得与赃物，绝非几年，而是已有许多代。”
    -_The Arabian Nights_. trans. Sir Richard F. Burton, 1885.

entries.english:
“Gravity, a mere nuisance to Christian, was a terror to Pope, Pagan, and
 Despair. To the mouse and any smaller animal it presents practically no
 dangers. You can drop a mouse down a thousand-yard mine shaft; and, on
 arriving at the bottom it gets a slight shock and walks away, provided
 that the ground is fairly soft. A rat is killed, a man is broken, a
 horse splashes.”
    -J.B.S. Haldane, “On Being The Right Size”. March 1926.
entries.translation:
“重力对基督徒不过是小小麻烦，对教皇、异教徒和绝望者却是恐怖。对鼠及更小动物而言，它几乎没有危险。把小鼠扔下一千码深的矿井，只要地面够软，它到底后稍稍一震，便能走开。大鼠会死，人会摔碎，马会溅开。”
    -J.B.S. Haldane, “On Being The Right Size”. March 1926.

entries.english:
“A tomb now suffices him for whom the world was not enough.”
    -Alexander the Great's epitaph.
entries.translation:
“整个世界尚不足以满足他，如今一座坟墓便已足够。”
    -Alexander the Great's epitaph.

entries.english:
“Out here in the zones, you never even knew when your bone marrow might book an
 exotic vacation and neglect to invite you along. Thinking square thoughts under
 a violet endomoon could redefine every third cell in your body as a verb. There
 were sneakers that ate feet, bifocals that ate eyeballs, strawberry yogurt that
 ate small intestines. Farther out there, _so_ much farther, there were
 wavelengths of something ancestral to light that could crawl into your past and
 eat the day you were born.

 Nobody so much as batted an eye or quivered a flange when these things happened
 to the unnaturally branchinated, the puzzling and comical tourists that blipped
 in and out from the forgettable grey. Things like herself, or Fern, or the
 plank maze loser were little more than _weird bugs_ to most entities, a quaint
 curiosity at best and more often an unwanted parasite. Infinite layers of
 reality, and it still felt, in the worst way, like she'd never left home.”
    -Jonathan Wojcik, _Awful Hospital_. 2021.
entries.translation:
“在这些区域，你甚至不知道骨髓何时会预订异国假期，却忘了邀请你。在紫色内月下思考方正的念头，可能把你身体中每第三个细胞重新定义成动词。有吃脚的运动鞋、吃眼球的双焦眼镜、吃小肠的草莓酸奶。更远、更远的地方，还有某种光之祖先的波长，能爬进过去，吃掉你出生的那一天。

这些事发生在那些不自然地长出枝杈、从容易遗忘的灰色中忽隐忽现的滑稽游客身上时，谁也不眨眼，不抖一下边缘。像她、蕨或木板迷宫输家这样的东西，对大多数存在不过是怪虫，最好也只是古怪奇观，通常则是不受欢迎的寄生物。现实有无限层，她却仍以最糟的方式觉得，自己从未离开家。”
    -Jonathan Wojcik, _Awful Hospital_. 2021.

entries.english:
ADDER, n. A species of snake. So called from its habit of adding funeral outlays
to the other expenses of living.
    -Ambrose Bierce, _The Devil's Dictionary_, 1906.
entries.translation:
蝰蛇，名词。一种蛇。其英文名 adder 源于它习惯在生活的其他开支上，再“加”一笔丧葬费。
    -Ambrose Bierce, _The Devil's Dictionary_, 1906.

entries.english:
Despite its unwieldy appearance, it is widely considered Alistair's most popular
work; countless variations of this spell can be found in surface libraries,
customised to prepare everything from floor polish to vegetable soup. In the
depths of the dungeon, however, most mages favor the combat utility of the
classic iteration.
entries.translation: 尽管外形笨重，这普遍被视为阿利斯泰尔最受欢迎的作品。地表图书馆能找到无数变体，按需求制备从地板蜡到蔬菜汤的一切。不过，在地牢深处，多数法师仍偏爱经典版本的战斗用途。

entries.english:
“Gringoire put out his hand for the little bag, but she drew back. ‘Do not
 touch it! It is an amulet, and either you will do mischief to the charm, or it
 will hurt you.’”
    -Victor Marie Hugo, _Notre Dame de Paris_, Book II, chapter VII “A Wedding
     Night”. 1831.
entries.translation:
“格兰古瓦伸手去拿小袋，她却退开。‘别碰！这是护身符，你不是会破坏咒力，就是会被它伤害。’”
    -Victor Marie Hugo, _Notre Dame de Paris_, Book II, chapter VII “A Wedding
     Night”. 1831.

entries.english:
“Remember, I am not recording the vision of a madman. The sun does not more
 certainly shine in the heavens, than that which I now affirm is true. Some
 miracle might have produced it, yet the stages of the discovery were distinct
 and probable. After days and nights of incredible labour and fatigue, I
 succeeded in discovering the cause of generation and life; nay, more, I became
 myself capable of bestowing animation upon lifeless matter.”
    -Mary Shelley, _Frankenstein, or the Modern Prometheus_,
     Vol. I, Chapter 3. 1818 (1st Ed.)
entries.translation:
“记住，我记录的不是疯人的幻象。太阳在天上照耀，也不比我此刻所说更确凿。也许是奇迹造成这一切，但发现的每个阶段都清楚而可信。经历不可思议的日夜劳作与疲惫后，我成功发现了生殖与生命的原因；不仅如此，我自己也能赋予无生命物质活力。”
    -Mary Shelley, _Frankenstein, or the Modern Prometheus_,
     Vol. I, Chapter 3. 1818 (1st Ed.)

entries.english:
“(Tell enters with his crossbow)
 W. TELL:
 My precious jewel now, —my chiefest treasure—
 A mark I'll set thee, which the cry of grief
 Could never penetrate,—but thou shalt pierce it,—
 And thou, my trusty bowstring, that so oft
 For sport has served me faithfully and well,
 Desert me not in this dread hour of need,—
 Only be true this once, my own good cord,
 That hast so often wing'd the biting shaft:—
 For shouldst thou fly successless from my hand,
 I have no second to send after thee.”
    -Friedrich Schiller, _Wilhelm Tell_, IV, iii. 1804.
     trans. Sir Theodore Martin, 1898.
entries.translation:
“（泰尔持弩入场）
泰尔：我珍贵的宝物，我最重要的珍藏，
我要为你指定一个目标，
悲伤的呼声穿不过它，你却必须穿透。
忠实的弓弦啊，你曾无数次
在游戏中忠诚地为我效劳，
别在这可怕的危急时刻抛弃我。
只需这一次准确，我的好弦，
你曾让锋利的箭飞出无数次；
若此箭从我手中徒劳飞走，
我再无第二箭可补。”
    -Friedrich Schiller, _Wilhelm Tell_, IV, iii. 1804.
     trans. Sir Theodore Martin, 1898.

entries.english:
“For myself, I have other occupations:  I make absurd matches; I marry
 greybeards with minors, masters with servants, girls with small fortunes with
 tender lovers who have none. It is I who introduced into this world luxury,
 debauchery, games of chance, and chemistry. I am the author of the first
 cookery book, the inventor of festivals, of dancing, music, plays, and of the
 newest fashions; in a word, I am ASMODEUS, surnamed The Devil on Two Sticks.”
    -Alain René Le Sage, _Asmodeus: Or, The Devil on Two Sticks_. 1707.
entries.translation:
“至于我，还有别的差事：安排荒唐婚姻，将白胡老人配给未成年人，主人配给仆役，有点嫁妆的姑娘配给一无所有的温柔情郎。奢华、放荡、赌博与化学，都是我引入人间。我写了第一本食谱，发明节庆、舞蹈、音乐、戏剧和最新时尚；一句话，我就是阿斯蒙蒂斯，别号双杖魔鬼。”
    -Alain René Le Sage, _Asmodeus: Or, The Devil on Two Sticks_. 1707.

entries.english:
“The fact is that I am unique. What a man can pass unto others does not
 interest me; like the philosopher, I think nothing is communicated by the art
 of writing. Annoying and trivial minutiae have no place in my spirit, a spirit
 which is receptive only to whatsoever is grand.”
  -Jorge Luis Borges, “The House of Asterion”. 1947.
   trans. Antonios Sarhanis, 2008.
entries.translation:
“事实上，我独一无二。人可以传授给他人的东西，我毫无兴趣；像那位哲人一样，我认为写作之术什么也传达不了。恼人而琐碎的细节，在我的精神里没有位置；我的精神只接纳宏伟之物。”
  -Jorge Luis Borges, “The House of Asterion”. 1947.
   trans. Antonios Sarhanis, 2008.

entries.english:
"A blacksmith shapes the heart of their steel just as much as any leader shapes
the hearts of their soldiers. If this armour of mine could speak, I know it
would say that we fight for the same cause."
entries.translation: “铁匠塑造钢铁之心，如同领袖塑造士兵之心。若我的护甲能说话，我知道它会说，我们为同一事业而战。”

entries.english:
“And Allah said,
 ‘As thou the deed hast done, so now the office shall be thine, O Azrael,
  to gather up for me the souls of men and women when their time has come;
  the souls of saints and sinners, of beggars and of princes,
  of the old or young, whate'er befall; and even though friends weep,
  and hearts of loved ones ache with sorrow and with anguish,
  when bereft of those they love.’
 So Azrael became the messenger of Death.”
    -J. E. Hanauer, _Folk-lore of the Holy Land, Moslem, Christian and Jewish_.
1907.
entries.translation:
“安拉说：
既然你做了此事，阿兹拉尔，这职责便归你。
人们时辰到了，你要替我收取男女灵魂，
圣人与罪人，乞丐与王侯，老人或年轻人，
无论何事发生；即使朋友哭泣，
亲人失去所爱，心中悲痛哀伤。
于是，阿兹拉尔成为死亡的使者。”
    -J. E. Hanauer, _Folk-lore of the Holy Land, Moslem, Christian and Jewish_.
1907.

entries.english:
“The republic always maintains seven or eight thousand regular troops on the
 frontiers, to prevent the incursions of the Tartars. The King does not
 maintain these troops; he only pays the Heydukes, the Semelles, and the
 Janizaries. The first-mentioned are dressed in blue, with large buttons and
 plates of tin, and have bonnets made of felt upon their heads. They have
 firelocks, and the bardiche, which they say is a very good weapon.”
    -John Pinkerton, _A General Collection of the Best and Most Interesting
     Voyages and Travels in all parts of the World, many of which are now first
     translated into English. Digested on a New Plan_. 1808.
entries.translation:
“共和国一直在边境维持七八千正规军，防备鞑靼人入侵。国王不供养这些军队，只支付海杜克、塞梅勒和禁卫军的费用。前者穿蓝衣，缀着大纽扣和锡片，头戴毡帽，装备火枪与长柄战斧；据说那是很好的武器。”
    -John Pinkerton, _A General Collection of the Best and Most Interesting
     Voyages and Travels in all parts of the World, many of which are now first
     translated into English. Digested on a New Plan_. 1808.

entries.english:
“Be thou like the imperial Basilisk
 Killing thy foe with unapparent wounds!
 Gaze on Oppression, till at that dread risk
 Aghast she pass from the Earth's disk:
 Fear not, but gaze—for freemen mightier grow,
 And slaves more feeble, gazing on their foe:—
 If Hope, and Truth, and Justice may avail,
 Thou shalt be great—All hail!”
    -Percy Bysshe Shelley, “Posthumous Poems”. 1824.
entries.translation:
“愿你如帝王般的蛇怪，
以看不见的伤口杀敌！
凝视压迫，直到她惊惶
从大地上消失。
别怕，只管凝视；自由人因凝视敌人更强，
奴隶却更弱。
若希望、真理与正义有用，
你必伟大——向你致敬！”
    -Percy Bysshe Shelley, “Posthumous Poems”. 1824.

entries.english:
“I'm your only friend
 I'm not your only friend
 But I'm a little glowing friend
 But really I'm not actually your friend
 But I am”
    -They Might Be Giants, “Birdhouse in Your Soul”. 1989.
entries.translation:
“我是你唯一的朋友，
我不是你唯一的朋友，
但我是个发光的小朋友，
可实际上我并非你的朋友，
但我又是。”
    -They Might Be Giants, “Birdhouse in Your Soul”. 1989.

entries.english:
“The Bès Kěmwar, “maggot spirit”, is one of the many _bès_ or disease spirits
 known to the Jah Hut of Malaysia. A polyvalent spirit, it is depicted as a
 maggot or caterpillar, with variants distinguished by hair, thorns, wings, and
 other details. It eats rice, vegetables, and other crops. It is responsible for
 aches in bones, joints, and muscles. If its caterpillar hair falls into water
 and that water is drunk, it causes coughing and bleeding in the throat. Maggot
 spirits are also known to live in rotten tree trunks and feed in them. Anyone
 who approaches the fallen tree will be bitten in the leg by the spirit, causing
 redness, swelling, and itching. All the toenails fall off but the swelling will
 be gone by two or three months.”
    - _A Book of Creatures_, 2020.
entries.translation:
“Bès Kěmwar，即‘蛆虫精灵’，是马来西亚 Jah Hut 人所知的众多 bès 疾病精灵之一。它形象多变，呈蛆或毛虫状，以毛、刺、翅膀等区别变体。它吃稻米、蔬菜及其他作物，引发骨、关节与肌肉疼痛。毛虫的毛落进水里，人喝了会咳嗽、喉咙出血。蛆虫精灵也住在腐树干中，以其为食。接近倒树者会被咬腿，发红、肿胀、发痒；脚趾甲全掉，肿胀则在两三个月后消退。”
    - _A Book of Creatures_, 2020.

entries.english:
“On leaf of palm, on sedge-wrought roll;
 On plastic clay and leathern scroll,
 Man wrote his thoughts; the ages passed,
 And lo! the Press was found at last!”
    -John Greenleaf Whittier, _The Library_, st. 4.
entries.translation:
“在棕榈叶上，在莎草卷上，
在可塑的泥土与皮革卷上，
人写下思想，岁月流逝，
看啊！印刷终于被发现！”
    -John Greenleaf Whittier, _The Library_, st. 4.

entries.english:
“Let who will boast their courage in the field,
 I find but little safety from my shield.
 Nature's, not honour's, law we must obey:
 This made me cast my useless shield away,
 And by a prudent flight and cunning save
 A life, which valour could not, from the grave.
 A better buckler I can soon regain;
 But who can get another life again?”
    -Archilochos. 7th cent. B.C.
     trans. William H. Goodwin, 1878.
entries.translation:
“任谁夸耀战场上的勇气，
我的盾却给不了多少安全。
该服从自然，而非荣誉的法则：
所以我丢掉无用盾牌，
以谨慎逃跑和机巧，
从坟墓中救回勇气救不了的命。
更好的盾很快能再得；
又有谁能再得一条命？”
    -Archilochos. 7th cent. B.C.
     trans. William H. Goodwin, 1878.

entries.english:
“And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the
 midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and
 the bush was not consumed.”
    -KJV Bible, Exodus 3:2.
entries.translation:
“耶和华的使者从荆棘中火焰里向他显现。他观看，见荆棘被火烧着，却没有烧毁。”
    -KJV Bible, Exodus 3:2.

entries.english:
“Happiness is a butterfly, which when pursued, is always just beyond your
 grasp, but which, if you will sit down quietly, may alight upon you.”
    -Nathaniel Hawthorne
entries.translation:
“幸福是蝴蝶，追逐时总在手边之外；若你安静坐下，它却可能落到你身上。”
    -Nathaniel Hawthorne

entries.english:
“There is shadow under this red rock,
 (Come in under the shadow of this red rock),
 And I will show you something different from either
 Your shadow at morning striding behind you
 Or your shadow at evening rising to meet you;
 I will show you fear in a handful of dust.”
    -T.S. Eliot, “The Waste Land”. 1922
entries.translation:
“这红岩下有阴影，
（来，到这红岩的阴影下），
我要给你看的，既不是
清晨在你身后阔步的影子，
也不是黄昏起身迎你的影子；
我要让你看见，一把尘土里的恐惧。”
    -T.S. Eliot, “The Waste Land”. 1922

entries.english:
“So passed he over into the island, taking with him the two brothers of
 Anaxius; where he found the forsaken knight attired in his own livery, as
 black as sorrow itself could see itself in the blackest glass: his ornaments
 of the same hue, but formd into the figures of ravens which seemed to gape for
 carrion: only his reins were snakes, which finely wrapping themselves one
 within the other, their heads came together to the cheeks and bosses of the
 bit, where they might seem to bite at the horse, and the horse, as he champed
 the bit, to bite at them, and that the white foam was engendered by the
 poisonous fury of the combat. His impresa was a Catoblepta, which so long lies
 dead as the moon (whereto it hath so natural a sympathy) wants her light. The
 word signified, that the moon wanted not the light, but the poor beast wanted
 the moon's light.”
    -Sir Philip Sidney
entries.translation:
“他带着阿纳克修斯两兄弟渡到岛上，发现那被遗弃的骑士穿着自己的号衣，黑得如悲伤在最黑镜中所见自身。装饰同样黑，却铸成张口等腐肉的乌鸦；缰绳则是相互盘绕的蛇，蛇头聚在嚼口两旁，仿佛咬马，马嚼衔时也像咬蛇，白沫仿佛来自这场战斗的毒怒。徽记是一只卡托布莱帕：它与月亮天然相感，月失光时便如死去。题辞意为，缺的并非月自身之光，而是可怜野兽所需的月光。”
    -Sir Philip Sidney

entries.english:
“And when Miranda sang
 Everyone turned away
 Used to the noose, they obey”
    -The Mars Volta, “Miranda That Ghost Just Isn't Holy Anymore”. 2005.
entries.translation:
“米兰达唱起歌时，
人人转过身去。
他们习惯了绞索，便服从。”
    -The Mars Volta, “Miranda That Ghost Just Isn't Holy Anymore”. 2005.

entries.english: <leather armour>
entries.translation: <leather armour>

entries.english:
“He held up his hand, and they all stopped, and I thought he seemed to be
 saying, ‘All these lives will I give you, ay, and many more and greater,
 through countless ages, if you will fall down and worship me!’ And then a red
 cloud, like the colour of blood, seemed to close over my eyes, and before I
 knew what I was doing, I found myself opening the sash and saying to Him,
 ‘Come in, Lord and Master!’”
    -Bram Stoker, _Dracula_. 1897.
entries.translation:
“他举起手，它们便都停下。我觉得他似乎在说：‘只要你跪下崇拜我，我就把这些生命赐给你，没错，还有更多更伟大的生命，绵延无数世代！’随后，一片血色红云仿佛遮住我的双眼。还不知自己在做什么，我已经打开窗扇，对他说：‘请进，主啊，我的主人！’”
    -Bram Stoker, _Dracula_. 1897.

entries.english:
“The glory of Yahweh mounted up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold
 of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full
 of the brightness of Yahweh's glory.

 The sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard even to the outer court, as
 the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.”
    -WEB Bible, Ezekiel 10:4-5
entries.translation:
“耶和华的荣耀从基路伯升起，停在殿门槛上，殿内充满云，院中满是荣耀的光。

基路伯的翅声传到外院，如全能神说话的声音。”
    -WEB Bible, Ezekiel 10:4-5

entries.english:
“In its simplest form it is a bird of the night, an owl (_Strix rufipes_) that
 flies on silent wings during the night to announce illness, death, or some
 other unwelcome event. When its croaking is heard it is advised to throw ash
 into the air and utter a few prayers in the hopes of turning away its evil.

 The chonchón is also said to be a _calcu_ or evil sorcerer in disguise. It
 resemble a human head, with oversized wing-like ears that allow it to fly.
 During the night, these sorcerers’ heads detach themselves from their bodies
 and fly around to cause mischief, invisible to most, their ominous _tué, tué,
 tué_ call announcing misfortune. They have the same powers as sorcerers do,
 and have been known to suck the blood of sleepers.”
    - _A Book of Creatures_, 2015.
entries.translation:
“最简单的形态，是一只夜鸟、棕林鸮（Strix rufipes），夜间无声飞翔，宣告疾病、死亡或其他不幸。听见沙哑叫声时，宜向空中撒灰并祈祷，希望驱走邪恶。

据说琼琼也是伪装的 calcu 邪术师，形如人头，巨大的翼状耳朵使其飞行。夜晚，术士的头脱离身体，四处作祟，多数人看不见，只有不祥的 tué、tué、tué 声预示厄运。它们拥有术士之力，也会吸饮熟睡者的血。”
    - _A Book of Creatures_, 2015.

entries.english:
“O Bell my wife, why dost thou flyte?
   Now is now, and then was then:
 Seek now all the world throughout,
   Thou kens not clowns from gentlemen:
 They are clad in black, green, yellow and blue,
   So far above their own degree.
 Once in my life I'll take a view;
   For I'll have a new cloak about me.”
    -Anonymous, “The Old Cloak”. 16th Century.
entries.translation:
“贝尔，我的妻，你为何责骂？
如今是如今，从前是从前。
遍寻世界，你也难分
乡人和绅士。
他们穿黑、绿、黄、蓝，
远远越过自己的身份。
我这辈子也要开开眼，
给自己披一件新斗篷。”
    -Anonymous, “The Old Cloak”. 16th Century.

entries.english:
“I fumbled to the window to experience the world
 And to hear my Madness singing, sitting on the kerbstone
 [A blind old drunken man who sings and mutters,
  With broken boot heels stained in many gutters]
 And as he sang the world began to fall apart . . .”
    -T.S. Eliot, “Prufrock's Pervigilium”. 1912 (published 1996).
entries.translation:
“我摸索到窗边，想感受世界，
听我的疯狂坐在路缘石上歌唱。
［一个失明、衰老、醉醺醺的人，唱着又低语，
破靴跟沾过许多阴沟。］
随着他的歌声，世界开始分崩离析……”
    -T.S. Eliot, “Prufrock's Pervigilium”. 1912 (published 1996).

entries.english:
“There was an Old Man with a beard,
 Who said, ‘It is just as I feared!
 Two Owls and a Hen,
 Four Larks and a Wren,
 Have all built their nests in my beard!’”
    -Edward Lear, _A Book of Nonsense [No. 1]_. 1846.
entries.translation:
“有位留胡子的老人说：
果然如我所怕！
两只猫头鹰、一只母鸡，
四只云雀、一只鹪鹩，
全在我的胡子里筑巢啦！”
    -Edward Lear, _A Book of Nonsense [No. 1]_. 1846.

entries.english:
“Unbearable, isn't it? The suffering of strangers, the agony of friends. There
 is a secret song at the center of the world, Joey, and its sound is like
 razors through flesh.”
    -Pinhead, _Hellraiser 3: Hell on Earth_. 1992.
entries.translation:
“难以忍受，是不是？陌生人的苦难，朋友的痛楚。乔伊，世界中心有一首秘密的歌，它的声音如剃刀划过血肉。”
    -Pinhead, _Hellraiser 3: Hell on Earth_. 1992.

entries.english:
“Good friend for Jesus’ sake forbear,
 To dig the dust enclosed here.
 Blessed be the man that spares these stones,
 And cursed be he that moves my bones.”
    -Epitaph on William Shakespeare's grave
entries.translation:
“好朋友，看在耶稣分上，
别挖这里封存的尘土。
留下这些石头者有福，
挪动我骨头者受诅。”
    -Epitaph on William Shakespeare's grave

entries.english:
“Between these twain the Daevas also chose not aright, for infatuation came
 upon them as they took counsel together, so that they chose the Worst Thought.
 Then they rushed together to Violence, that they might enfeeble the world of
 men.”
    -the Avesta, Yasna XXX, 6, Ahunavaiti Gatha.
    trans. Christian Bartholomae, 1951.
entries.translation:
“在两者之间，诸魔也未作正确选择；它们商议时受到迷妄，于是选择最恶之念。随后一同投向暴力，企图削弱人间世界。”
    -the Avesta, Yasna XXX, 6, Ahunavaiti Gatha.
    trans. Christian Bartholomae, 1951.

entries.english:
“At these words he started up, and beheld—not his Sophia—no, nor a Circassian
 maid richly and elegantly attired for the grand Signior's seraglio. No;
 without a gown, in a shift that was somewhat of the coarsest, and none of the
 cleanest, bedewed likewise with some odoriferous effluvia, the produce of the
 day's labour, with a pitchfork in her hand, Molly Seagrim approached.”
    -Henry Fielding, _The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling_, Book V, ch. X.
     1749.
entries.translation:
“听见这话，他跳起来，看见的不是索菲娅，也不是为苏丹后宫打扮得华丽优雅的切尔克斯少女。不，走来的是莫莉·西格里姆：没穿长裙，只着粗糙且不太干净的衬衣，沾着一日劳作留下的气味，手里还拿着干草叉。”
    -Henry Fielding, _The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling_, Book V, ch. X.
     1749.

entries.english:
“As one example of the meanings inherent in a form, let us examine a particular
 form of vertical stone marker, variously called stele, obelisk, standing-stone,
 and memorial column. These have been historically and commonly used to
 commemorate honored phenomena. So, when a people wish to remember an important
 relationship, event or personage, a location is dedicated to it and often
 marked with an enduring and aspiring vertical form or sets of them. In natural
 language, a vertical stone means: an aspiring connector between us (on earth)
 and an ideal (up there); that we ‘stand up’ with pride about this honored
 phenomenon. The marker is a symbolic inhabitation of the place it occupies. Its
 size and workmanship is a sacrifice of much work and resources to a memory. It
 is a strong suggestion (because we left it to them and it is of durable
 material) that future people also give honor to the memorialized phenomenon.
 When we use this particular physical form of the vertical marker, both its
 historic use as an honorific and its meanings in natural language may well send
 a message that this is an honored place, a place about a ‘good’ both in our
 culture and in the culture of future observers.”
    -“Expert Judgment on Markers to Deter Inadvertent Human Intrusion into the
      Waste Isolation Pilot Plant”, Sandia National Laboratories report. 1993
entries.translation:
“以形态内含的意义为例，考察称作石碑、方尖碑、立石或纪念柱的竖直石标。历史上，它们通常用来纪念受尊崇之事。人们想记住重要关系、事件或人物时，会指定地点，常竖起耐久、向上的形体。自然语言中，立石意味着我们在地上与上方理想之间的奋起连接，也意味着为受敬重之事骄傲地站立。标志象征性占据其所在地点；大小与工艺，是为记忆献出大量劳力和资源。耐久材料和留给后人的事实，还强烈暗示未来人也应尊崇所纪念之物。因此，使用这种竖直标记，其历史上的尊荣用途及自然语言意义，很可能传达：此地值得敬重；无论对我们的文化还是未来观察者，这里都关乎一种‘善’。”
    -“Expert Judgment on Markers to Deter Inadvertent Human Intrusion into the
      Waste Isolation Pilot Plant”, Sandia National Laboratories report. 1993

entries.english:
“‘Ah! ah! ah!’ laughed his two men, ‘how the Norman villains will be humbled
when they see their doughty knight's skull beaten in by our brave countryman.’”
    -_Tales of Chivalry; or, Perils by Flood and Field_. 1830.
entries.translation:
“哈哈哈！”两名手下笑道，“看见勇武骑士的脑袋被我们勇敢同胞砸凹，那些诺曼恶棍该有多丢脸！”
    -_Tales of Chivalry; or, Perils by Flood and Field_. 1830.

entries.english:
“Hoc idem magis ostendit antiquius Iovis nomen: nam olim Diovis et Diespiter
 dictus, id est dies pater; a quo dei dicti qui inde, et dius et divum, unde
 sub divo, Dius Fidius. Itaque inde eius perforatum tectum, ut ea videatur
 divum, id est caelum. Quidam negant sub tecto per hunc deierare oportere.
 Aelius Dium Fidium dicebat Diovis filium, ut Graeci Dioskopon Castorem, et
 putabat hunc esse Sancum ab Sabina lingua et Herculem a Graeca. Idem hic Dis
 pater dicitur infimus, qui est coniunctus terrae, ubi omnia ut oriuntur ita
 aboriuntur; quorum quod finis ortuum, Orcus dictus.”
    -Marcus Terentius Varro, _De Lingua Latina_, Liber V, circa 40 BC.
entries.translation:
“朱庇特更古老的名字更能表明这一点：从前称 Diovis 和 Diespiter，即‘白昼之父’；诸神、神圣以及天空等词由此得名，露天之说及 Dius Fidius 之名也与此有关。因此，他的殿顶开有孔，使人可看见 divum，也就是天空。有些人否认应该在屋顶下以此神起誓。埃利乌斯说，Dius Fidius 是 Diovis 之子，如希腊人的狄俄斯库里卡斯托尔；又认为他就是萨宾语的 Sancus 和希腊人的赫拉克勒斯。最下方的神又称 Dis Pater，与大地相连，万物从那里生，也在那里亡；因他是诞生的终点，又被称作 Orcus。”
    -Marcus Terentius Varro, _De Lingua Latina_, Liber V, circa 40 BC.

entries.english:
“Skill and grace, the twin brother and sister, are dancing playfully on your
 finger tips.”
    -Rabindranath Tagore, _Chitra_, Act I, Scene iv. 1914.
entries.translation:
“技巧与优雅，这对孪生兄妹，正在你的指尖嬉戏起舞。”
    -Rabindranath Tagore, _Chitra_, Act I, Scene iv. 1914.

entries.english:
“How undisturbed, the sleep of the foolish.”
    -Philip K. Dick
entries.translation:
“愚人睡得多安稳。”
    -Philip K. Dick

entries.english: <dreamshard necklace>
entries.translation: <dreamshard necklace>

entries.english:
DUEL, n. A formal ceremony preliminary to the reconciliation of two enemies.
Great skill is necessary to its satisfactory observance; if awkwardly
performed the most unexpected and deplorable consequences sometimes ensue.
A long time ago, a man lost his life in a duel.
    -Ambrose Bierce, _The Devil's Dictionary_, 1906.
entries.translation:
决斗，名词。两位敌人和解之前举行的正式仪式。要圆满遵行，需要极高技巧；若执行笨拙，有时会产生极为意外而可悲的后果。很久以前，有个人在决斗中丢了性命。
    -Ambrose Bierce, _The Devil's Dictionary_, 1906.

entries.english:
“When the hoopoe returned to Solomon (he told him the news), and he responded
 (to Sheba's people): “Are you giving me money? What GOD has given me is far
 better than what He has given you. You are the ones to rejoice in such gifts.”
 (To the hoopoe, he said), “Go back to them (and let them know that) we will
 come to them with forces they cannot imagine. We will evict them, humiliated
 and debased.” He said, “O you elders, which of you can bring me her mansion,
 before they arrive here as submitters?” One afrit from the jinns said, “I can
 bring it to you before you stand up. I am powerful enough to do this.”
    -The Quran, Sura 27 Al-Naml
entries.translation:
“戴胜鸟回到所罗门那里报告消息，他答复示巴人：你们用钱财赠我？真主给我的，远胜给你们的，你们才为这种礼物欢喜。他又吩咐戴胜鸟：回去告诉他们，我们将带来他们无法想象的军队，屈辱地将他们驱逐。他问长老：他们归顺到来前，你们谁能把她的宫殿带来？精灵中的一位强者说：我能在你起身前带来，我有足够力量。”
    -The Quran, Sura 27 Al-Naml

entries.english:
“No sooner had sleep caught him, dissolving all his grief
 as mists of refreshing slumber poured around him there—
 his powerful frame was bone-weary from charging Hector
 straight and hard to the walls of windswept Troy—
 than the ghost of stricken Patroclus drifted up...
 He was like the man to the life, every feature,
 the same tall build and the fine eyes and voice
 and the very robes that used to clothe his body.
 Hovering at his head the phantom rose and spoke:
 ‘Sleeping, Achilles? You’ve forgotten me, my friend.
 You never neglected me in life, only now in death.
 Bury me, quickly—let me pass the Gates of Hades.
 They hold me off at a distance, all the souls,
 the shades of the burnt-out, breathless dead,
 never to let me cross the river, mingle with them...
 They leave me to wander up and down, abandoned, lost
 at the House of Death with the all-embracing gates.’”
    -Homer, _The Iliad_, XXIII, 72-88.
     trans. Robert Fagles, 1990.
entries.translation:
“睡眠刚攫住他，清新睡雾消去悲伤——
他曾猛烈追赶赫克托耳至风扫特洛伊城墙，
强健躯体已疲惫入骨——
死去帕特罗克洛斯的鬼魂便飘来。
容貌、身高、俊眼、声音，
乃至衣袍，都与生前无异。
幻影悬在头边，说：
‘睡着吗，阿喀琉斯？朋友，你忘了我。
生前从未冷落我，死后却如此。
快埋葬我，让我越过冥府之门。
死去、烧尽、失去呼吸的魂灵把我远远挡住，
不许渡河，不许与它们相聚。
我只能被遗弃、迷失地游荡，
在容纳一切的死亡宫门外。’”
    -Homer, _The Iliad_, XXIII, 72-88.
     trans. Robert Fagles, 1990.

entries.english:
“SEE! warp is stretched
 For warrior’s fall;
 Lo, weft in loom,
 ’Tis wet with blood;
 Now, fight foreboding,
 ’Neath friends’ swift fingers
 Our gray woof waxeth
 With war’s alarms,
 Our warp blood-red,
 Our weft corse-blue.

 This woof is y-woven
 With entrails of men;
 This warp is hard weighted
 With heads of the slain;
 Spears blood-besprinkled
 For spindles we use,
 Our loom iron-bound,
 And arrows our reels;
 With swords for our shuttles
 This war-woof we work;
 So weave we, weird sisters,
 Our war-winning woof.

 Now war-winner walketh
 To weave in her turn,
 Now Sword-swinger steppeth,
 Now Swift-stroke, now Storm;
 When they speed the shuttle
 How spear-heads shall flash!
 Shields crash, and helm-gnawer
 On harness bite hard!”
    -_The Story of Burnt Njal_, trans. George Dasent. 1861
entries.translation:
“看！经线已张，为战士倒下而织；
织机纬线湿透鲜血。
朋友快指下，灰布随战警而长，
经线血红，纬线尸青。

这布以人的肠子织成，
经线坠着死者头颅；
血溅长矛作纺锤，
铁箍织机，箭作卷轴，
剑作梭子，织这战争之布。
我们，命运姐妹，织出制胜的布。

赢战者前来轮织，
挥剑者、迅击者、风暴相继迈步。
梭子疾飞时，矛尖将闪耀，
盾牌碎裂，啃盔之刃
狠狠咬入甲胄！”
    -_The Story of Burnt Njal_, trans. George Dasent. 1861

entries.english:
“‘But I am frightened of what is dark, urZah.’

 ‘With reason,’ the urRu replied. ‘Darkness imprisons the light. Darkness
  destroys all beings, covets all energy. It is evil.’

 ‘What is evil?’ Jen asked.

 ‘Evil does not exist,’ urZah answered. ‘Evil is disharmony between existences.
  Now go, Gelfling, with your questions.’”
    -A. C. H. Smith, _Jim Henson’s “The Dark Crystal”: The Novelization_. 1982.
entries.translation:
“可是我害怕黑暗，乌尔扎。”

“有道理，”乌尔鲁答道，“黑暗囚禁光，毁灭一切生命，觊觎所有能量。它是邪恶。”

“什么是邪恶？”詹问。

“邪恶并不存在，”乌尔扎说，“邪恶是存在之间的不和谐。现在，格尔弗林人，带着你的问题走吧。”
    -A. C. H. Smith, _Jim Henson’s “The Dark Crystal”: The Novelization_. 1982.

entries.english:
“She danced, and was compelled to dance—to dance in the dark night. The shoes
 carried her on over thorn and brier; she scratched herself till she bled; she
 danced away across the heath to a little lonely house. Here she knew the
 executioner dwelt; and she tapped with her fingers on the panes, and
 called,—‘Come out, come out! I cannot come in, for I must dance!’

 And the Executioner said,—‘You probably don't know who I am? I cut off the bad
 people's heads with my axe, and mark how my axe rings!’

 ‘Do not strike off my head,’ said Karen, ‘for if you do I cannot repent of my
 sin. But strike off my feet with the red shoes?’

 And then she confessed all her sin, and the Executioner cut off her feet with
 the red shoes; but the shoes danced away with the little feet over the fields
 and into the deep forest.

 And he cut her a pair of wooden feet, with crutches, and taught her a psalm,
 which the criminals always sing; and she kissed the hand that had held the
 axe, and went away across the heath.”
    -Hans Christian Andersen, “The Red Shoes”, _Nye Eventyr. Første Bind.
     Tredie Samling._. 1845.
entries.translation:
“她跳舞，被迫在黑夜中跳舞。鞋带她穿过荆棘，划得鲜血直流；她跳过荒原，来到孤零零的小屋。她知道刽子手住在那里，便叩窗呼喊：‘出来，出来！我进不去，我必须跳舞！’

刽子手说：‘你大概不知道我是谁？我用斧头砍坏人的脑袋，听我的斧子多响！’

‘别砍我的头，’卡伦说，‘否则我无法为罪悔改。但砍下穿红鞋的双脚吧？’

她承认一切罪，刽子手砍下穿红鞋的脚；鞋却带着小脚跳过田野，进入深林。

他又给她做木脚和拐杖，教一首罪犯常唱的圣歌。她亲吻持斧的手，穿过荒原离去。”
    -Hans Christian Andersen, “The Red Shoes”, _Nye Eventyr. Første Bind.
     Tredie Samling._. 1845.

entries.english:
“Even after forcing their way, with great effort and loss, through this double
 defence, [the Germans] still found themselves at a disadvantage; for their
 armour scarce enabled them to contend on equal terms with the uncouth but
 formidable weapons of their adversaries. The Bohemians were armed with long
 iron flails, which they swung with prodigious force. They seldom failed to
 hit, and when they did so, the flail crashed through brazen helmet, skull and
 all.”
    -James A. Wylie, _The History of Protestantism_, vol. I, book 3, ch. 15
     “John Huss and the Hussite Wars”. 1878.
entries.translation:
“德军付出巨大努力与伤亡，突破双重防线后仍处下风，因为铠甲不足以抗衡对手粗陋却可怕的武器。波希米亚人装备长铁连枷，挥舞时力大惊人，极少落空。命中时，连枷连铜盔、头骨一并砸穿。”
    -James A. Wylie, _The History of Protestantism_, vol. I, book 3, ch. 15
     “John Huss and the Hussite Wars”. 1878.

entries.english:
“From this story it is evident that in former times the jellyfish once had a
shell and bones something like a tortoise, but, ever since the Dragon King's
sentence was carried out on the ancestor of the jelly fishes, his descendants
have all been soft and boneless just as you see them to-day thrown up by the
waves high upon the shores of Japan.”
    -“The Jellyfish and the Monkey”, adapted by Yei Theodora Ozaki, _Young
     Folk's Treasury_, vol. II. 1909.
entries.translation:
“故事清楚表明，水母从前也像龟，有壳有骨。但自龙王判决在水母祖先身上执行后，它的后代便都柔软无骨，正如如今被海浪冲上日本岸边的模样。”
    -“The Jellyfish and the Monkey”, adapted by Yei Theodora Ozaki, _Young
     Folk's Treasury_, vol. II. 1909.

entries.english:
“Khrysaor, married to Kallirhoe, daughter of glorious Okeanos, was father to
 the triple-headed Geryon, but Geryon was killed by the great strength of
 Herakles at sea-circled Erytheis beside his own shambling cattle on that day
 when Herakles drove those broad-faced cattle toward holy Tiryns, when he
 crossed the stream of Okeanos and had killed Orthos and the oxherd Eurytion
 out in the gloomy meadow beyond fabulous Okeanos.”
    -Hesiod, _Theogony_, circa 700 BCE.
entries.translation:
“克律萨俄耳娶光荣俄刻阿诺斯之女卡利罗厄，生下三头革律翁。后来，赫拉克勒斯渡过俄刻阿诺斯河，在远方昏暗牧场杀死奥尔托斯与牧人欧律提翁，将宽额牛群赶往神圣提任斯；也在环海厄律忒亚，凭伟力将革律翁杀死在他踉跄行走的牛群旁。”
    -Hesiod, _Theogony_, circa 700 BCE.

entries.english:
“Therewith the gyant buckled him to fight,
 Inflamd with scornefull wrath and high disdaine,
 And lifting up his dreadful club on hight,
 All armed with ragged snubbes and knottie graine,
 Him thought at first encounter to have slaine.”
    -Edmund Spenser, _The Faerie Queene_, Book I, “The Legend of the Knight of
     the Red Crosse”, Canto VIII, stanza vii, l. 55-9. 1590.
entries.translation:
“巨人随即整装迎战，
满怀轻蔑与狂怒，
高举骇人的木棒，
棒身遍布粗瘤与硬节，
以为一交手便能将他杀死。”
    -Edmund Spenser, _The Faerie Queene_, Book I, “The Legend of the Knight of
     the Red Crosse”, Canto VIII, stanza vii, l. 55-9. 1590.

entries.english:
“Or burst the vanish’d Hero’s lofty mound;
 Far on the solitary shore he sleeps:
 He fell, and falling nations mourn’d around;
 But now not one of saddening thousands weeps,
 Nor warlike worshipper his vigil keeps
 Where demi-gods appear’d, as records tell.
 Remove yon skull from out the scatter’d heaps:
 Is that a temple where a God may dwell?
 Why ev’n the worm at last disdains her shatter’d cell!

 Look on its broken arch, its ruin’d wall,
 Its chambers desolate, and portals foul:
 Yes, this was once Ambition’s airy hall,
 The dome of Thought, the palace of the Soul:
 Behold through each lack-lustre, eyeless hole,
 The gay recess of Wisdom and of Wit
 And Passion’s host, that never brook’d control:
 Can all saint, sage, or sophist ever writ,
 People this lonely tower, this tenement refit?”
    -Lord Byron, _Childe Harold's Pilgrimage_, Canto the Second, Stanzas V-VI
entries.translation:
“掘开逝去英雄高耸的坟冢，
他长眠在孤独海岸远方。
他倒下时，诸国哀悼，
如今成千上万悲伤者无一再哭，
也无尚武崇拜者守夜。
史书说，半神曾现于此。
从散乱骨堆取出那颗头骨：
那是可让神居住的殿堂吗？
如今连蛆虫也嫌弃这破屋！

看破拱、毁墙、空室与污门。
这里曾是野心的高堂，
思想的圆顶，灵魂的宫殿。
透过无光无眼的洞，
看见智慧、机敏的欢乐居所，
和从不服管束的激情。
圣徒、贤者与智辩者所有著述，
能重新住满孤塔、修复这间居所吗？”
    -Lord Byron, _Childe Harold's Pilgrimage_, Canto the Second, Stanzas V-VI

entries.english:
“To know the perfect length of your ſhort ſtaffe, or half Pike, Forreſt bil,
 Partiſan or Gleue, or ſuch like weapons of vantage and perfect lengths, you
 ſhall ſtand vpright, holding the ſtaffe vpright cloſe by your body, with your
 left hãd, reaching with your right hand your ſtaffe as high as you can, and
 then allow to that length a ſpace to ſet both your hands, when you come to
 fight, wherein you may conueniently ſtrike, thruſt and ward, & that is the
 iuſt length according to you ſtature. And this note, that theſe lengths will
 commonly fall out to be eight or nine foot long, and will fit, although not
 iuſt, the ſtatures of all men, without any hindrance at all vnto them in their
 fight, becauſe in any weapon wherin the hands may be remoued, and at libertie,
 to make the weapon lõger or ſhorter in fight at his pleaſure, a foot of the
 ſtaffe behind the backmoſt hand doth no harme.”
    -George Silver,_Paradoxes of Defence_.1599.
entries.translation:
“要确定短杖、半长枪、钩镰、戟或大刀等长柄武器最适合的长度，应站直，用左手贴身竖持长柄，右手尽可能向上够，再加上作战时容纳双手的长度，使挥击、刺击和格挡都便利。这便是符合身高的长度。通常约八九英尺，即使不完全吻合，也适合各种身材，不妨碍战斗。因为双手可自由移动，随意缩短或延长武器的有效长度，后手后方多出一英尺也无妨。”
    -George Silver,_Paradoxes of Defence_.1599.

entries.english:
“Then he descended softly and beckoned to Nuth. But the gnoles had watched him
 through knavish holes that they bore in trunks of the trees, and the unearthly
 silence gave way, as it were with a grace, to the rapid screams of Tonker as
 they picked him up from behind — screams that came faster and faster until
 they were incoherent. And where they took him it is not good to ask, and what
 they did with him I shall not say.”
    -Lord Dunsany, “How Nuth Would Have Practised His Art Upon the Gnoles”.
1912.
entries.translation:
“他轻轻下去，向纳思示意。但豺狼人已透过树干上狡猾的窥孔注视他。诡异寂静仿佛优雅退场，换成它们从背后抓起汤克时急促的惨叫，越来越快，最终不成声音。它们把他带去哪里，最好别问；对他做了什么，我不说。”
    -Lord Dunsany, “How Nuth Would Have Practised His Art Upon the Gnoles”.
1912.

entries.english:
“There will arise one named Feridoun, who shall inherit thy throne
 and reverse thy fortunes, and strike thee down with a cow-headed mace.”
    -Firdausi, _Shahnameh_. ca. 1000 A.D.
     trans. Helen Zimmern, 1883.
entries.translation:
“将有一人名费里敦兴起，
继承你的王座，逆转你的命运，
以牛头钉头锤将你击倒。”
    -Firdausi, _Shahnameh_. ca. 1000 A.D.
     trans. Helen Zimmern, 1883.

entries.english:
“And Diarmid oh, Diarmid he perished in the strife;
 His head it was spiked upon a halberd high;
 His colours they were trampled: he had no chance of life
 If the Lord God Himself stood by!—
  Och, ochone!”
    -James Clarence Mangan , _A Farewell to Patrick Sarsfield, Earl of Lucan_.
     ca. 1840.
entries.translation:
“迪尔米德啊，他战死了，
头被挑在高高长戟上；
旗帜遭践踏，纵使主亲临，
也再无生还希望！
啊，悲哉！”
    -James Clarence Mangan , _A Farewell to Patrick Sarsfield, Earl of Lucan_.
     ca. 1840.

entries.english:
“About her middle round
 A cry of Hell-hounds never-ceasing barked
 With wide Cerberean mouths full loud, and rung
 A hideous peal; yet, when they list, would creep,
 If aught disturbed their noise, into her womb,
 And kennel there; yet there still barked and howled
 Within unseen.”
    -John Milton, _Paradise Lost_, Book II, 1667.
entries.translation:
“她腰间一圈地狱犬，
以刻耳柏洛斯般的巨口不停狂吠，
响成可怕钟声。有时，
若有什么打断吠叫，它们便爬回子宫，
在里面筑窝，却仍在看不见处
狂吠、嚎叫。”
    -John Milton, _Paradise Lost_, Book II, 1667.

entries.english:
“Ok, let's review. It's up to the fair young maiden to rescue the dragon from
 the fire breathing knights in shining armour.”
    -Exiern
entries.translation:
“好，复习一下：这回该由美丽少女，把龙从喷火的闪甲骑士手中救出来。”
    -Exiern

entries.english:
“Fern came slowly down the stairs. Her eyes were red from crying. As she
 approached her chair, the carton wobbled, and there was a scratching noise.
 Fern looked at her father. Then she lifted the lid of the carton. There,
 inside, looking up at her, was the newborn pig. It was a white one. The
 morning light shone through its ears, turning them pink. “He's yours,” said
 Mr. Arable.  “Saved from an untimely death. And may the good Lord forgive me
 for this foolishness.”
    -E.B. White, _Charlotte's Web_
entries.translation:
“芬慢慢走下楼，眼睛哭红了。走近椅子时，纸箱晃动，传来抓挠声。她看父亲，再揭开箱盖。里面，一只新生小猪抬头看她，白白的，晨光透过耳朵，染成粉红。阿拉布尔先生说：它归你了，从夭折中救回来。愿主原谅我这愚行。”
    -E.B. White, _Charlotte's Web_

entries.english:
“We have lingered in the chambers of the sea
 By sea-girls wreathed with seaweed red and brown
 Till human voices wake us, and we drown.”
    -T.S. Eliot, _The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock_. lines 129-131. 1915.
entries.translation:
“我们曾流连海的宫室，
身旁海女缠着红褐海草，
直到人声唤醒我们，而我们淹没。”
    -T.S. Eliot, _The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock_. lines 129-131. 1915.

entries.english:
“Suppose you found your brother in bed with your wife, and put a javelin
 through both of them, you would be justified, and they would atone for their
 sins, and be received into the kingdom of God.”
    -Brigham Young, _Journal of Discourses_, 3:247. 1856.
entries.translation:
“假如发现兄弟与你妻子同床，用一支标枪把两人一并贯穿，你是正当的。他们也会偿还罪过，被接纳进上帝之国。”
    -Brigham Young, _Journal of Discourses_, 3:247. 1856.

entries.english:
“And then I looked farther, beyond the pallid line of the sands, and I saw a
 Pyramid of gold, the wonder Khufu had built. As a golden wonder it saluted me,
 as a golden thing it greeted me, as a golden miracle I shall remember it.”
    -Robert Hichens, _The Spell of Egypt_. 1910.
entries.translation:
“我越过苍白的沙线向远处看，见到一座黄金金字塔，胡夫建造的奇迹。它以黄金奇观向我致意，以黄金之物迎接我；我将永远记住这黄金奇迹。”
    -Robert Hichens, _The Spell of Egypt_. 1910.

entries.english:
“...for the shield may be as important for victory, as the sword or spear.”
    -Charles Darwin, “The Origin of Species”. 1859.
entries.translation:
“……盾对于胜利，也许和剑或矛一样重要。”
    -Charles Darwin, “The Origin of Species”. 1859.

entries.english:
“... Kraken, also called the Crab-fish, which [according to the pilots of
 Norway] is not that huge, for heads and tails counted, he is no larger than
 our Öland is wide [i.e. less than 16 km] ... He stays at the sea floor,
 constantly surrounded by innumerable small fishes, who serve as his food and
 are fed by him in return: for his meal, if I remember correctly what E.
 Pontoppidan writes, lasts no longer than three months, and another three are
 then needed to digest it. His excrements nurture in the following an army of
 lesser fish, and for this reason, fishermen plumb after his resting place ...
 Gradually, Kraken ascends to the surface, and when he is at ten to twelve
 fathoms, the boats had better move out of his vicinity, as he will shortly
 thereafter burst up, like a floating island, spurting water from his dreadful
 nostrils and making ring waves around him, which can reach many miles. Could
 one doubt that this is the Leviathan of Job?”
    -Jacob Wallenberg, “Min son på galejan”. 1781.
entries.translation:
“克拉肯，又称蟹鱼，据挪威领航员说并不算大：连头带尾，也不过厄兰岛那么宽，不到十六公里。它卧在海底，被无数小鱼包围，吃鱼，也反过来养鱼。据我记得蓬托皮丹所写，一餐不超过三个月，再用三个月消化；排泄物滋养小鱼大军，因此渔人测深寻找其栖处。它渐渐上浮，到水深十至十二噚时，船最好远离，因为它很快会像浮岛冲出水面，从可怕鼻孔喷水，激起延伸数英里的环浪。谁还能怀疑，这就是约伯的利维坦？”
    -Jacob Wallenberg, “Min son på galejan”. 1781.

entries.english:
“A weapon that comes down as still
 As snowflakes fall upon the sod;
 But executes a freeman's will,
 As lightning does the will of God.”
    -John Pierpont, “The Ballot”. ca. 1850.
entries.translation:
“它落下时静默，
如雪片落在草地；
却执行自由人的意志，
如闪电执行上帝之意。”
    -John Pierpont, “The Ballot”. ca. 1850.

entries.english:
“Now the house was full of men and women; and all the lords of the Philistines
 were there; and there were upon the roof about three thousand men and women,
 that beheld while Samson made sport.

 And Samson called unto the LORD, and said, O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray
 thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at
 once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.

 And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, and
 on which it was borne up, of the one with his right hand, and of the other
 with his left.

 And Samson said, Let me die with the Philistines. And he bowed himself with
 all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that
 were therein. So the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which
 he slew in his life.”
    -KJV Bible, Judges 16:27-30.
entries.translation:
“屋里挤满男女，非利士众首领也在那里。屋顶约有三千男女，看参孙表演。

参孙求告耶和华说：主耶和华啊，求你记念我，再赐我这一次力量，使我向非利士人报双眼之仇。

参孙抱住支撑房屋的两根中央柱子，一根用右手，一根用左手。

他说：让我与非利士人同死吧！便尽力屈身，房屋倒在首领和众人身上。这样，他临死杀的人，比一生杀的还多。”
    -KJV Bible, Judges 16:27-30.

entries.english:
“The second Labour which he undertook was the slaying of the Lernaian Hydra,
 springing from whose single body were fashioned a hundred necks, each bearing
 the head of a serpent. And when one head was cut off, the place where it was
 severed put forth two others; for this reason it was considered to be
 invincible, and with good reason, since the part of it which was subdued sent
 forth a two-fold assistance in its place. Against a thing so difficult to
 manage as this Herakles devised an ingenious scheme and commanded Iolaos to
 sear with a burning brand the part which had been severed, in order to check
 the flow of the blood.”
    -Diodorus Siculus, _Bibliotheca Historica_. [4. 11. 5.]. c. 100.
entries.translation:
“他的第二项功业是杀死勒尔那海德拉，一个躯干长出一百条脖子，每条都有蛇头。砍掉一头，断处便生出两个，所以它理所当然被视为不可战胜：每被制服一处，就有双倍支援代替。为应付这难缠怪物，赫拉克勒斯想出巧计，命伊奥拉俄斯以火把灼烧断口，止住血流。”
    -Diodorus Siculus, _Bibliotheca Historica_. [4. 11. 5.]. c. 100.

entries.english:
“Freilich verbürgt uns keine Silbe die Existenz von solcherlei Thieren, wenn
 wir uns den Drachen oder Lindwurm als ein Ungeheuer vorstellen, dessen langer
 Hals in einen Adler-, Löwen- oder Delphinenkopf endigt; das auf dem breiten
 Rücken Greifs- oder Nachisittige trägt; und am vielfach
 gerollten Schweif einen Stachel mit Widerhaken hat; Feuer speit; sich in
 Mädchen verliebt und diese entführt; bald diese bald jene Gestalt annimmt; auf
 sauer erworbenen Schatzen ruht — kurz, als ein Ungeheuer, das alle
 Eigenschaften besitzt, welche die Fabel ihm andichtet; dann wäre es Wahnsinn,
 an Drachen und Lindwürmer glauben zu wollen. Nehmen wir aber dafür bloß ein
 furchtbares Ungeheuer überhaupt, welches nun aus unserem Welttheile vertilgt
 ist, so hat der Glaube daran nichts Lächerliches.”
    -Leopold Ziegelhauſer, _Schattenbilder der Vorzeit: Ein Kranz von
     Geschichten, Sagen, Legenden, Märchen, Skizzen und Heldenmahlen, Aus allen
     Gegenden Deutschlands und des österreichischen Kaiserstaates_. 1844.
entries.translation:
“若把龙想成长颈尽头接鹰、狮或海豚头，阔背生狮鹫或其他翅膀，盘尾带倒钩，喷火，爱上并掳走少女，随意变形，趴在辛苦积来的宝藏上，总之拥有传说赋予的一切特征的怪物，那么没有一个字能保证它存在，相信它便是疯狂。但若只指一种可怕、如今已从我们这片世界灭绝的巨兽，相信它便没有什么可笑。”
    -Leopold Ziegelhauſer, _Schattenbilder der Vorzeit: Ein Kranz von
     Geschichten, Sagen, Legenden, Märchen, Skizzen und Heldenmahlen, Aus allen
     Gegenden Deutschlands und des österreichischen Kaiserstaates_. 1844.

entries.english:
“[My plan] does not propose to fill your lobby with squabbling colony agents,
 who will require the interposition of your mace at every instant to keep the
 peace among them.”
    -Edmund Burke, “On Conciliation with America”, speech in Parliament. 1775.
entries.translation:
“我的计划并不是让争吵不休的殖民地代理人挤满大厅，逼得你每时每刻都得动用权杖来维持和平。”
    -Edmund Burke, “On Conciliation with America”, speech in Parliament. 1775.

entries.english:
“Ctesias writeth, that in Aethiopia likewise there is a beast which he calleth
 Mantichora, having three rankes of teeth, which when they meet togither are
 let in one within another like the teeth of combes: with the face and eares of
 a man, with red eyes; of colour sanguine, bodied like a lyon, and having a
 taile armed with a sting like a scorpion: his voice resembleth the noise of a
 flute and trumpet sounded together: very swift he is, and mans flesh of all
 others hee most desireth.”
    -Pliny the Elder, _Natural History_, Book 8, Chapter XXI
entries.translation:
“克忒西亚斯说，埃塞俄比亚有兽名蝎尾狮，牙有三排，合起时像梳齿彼此嵌入；人面人耳，红眼，血色，狮身，尾带蝎刺；声音如笛与号同响，行动极快，所有肉中最爱人肉。”
    -Pliny the Elder, _Natural History_, Book 8, Chapter XXI

entries.english:
“This night the Lord of Illusion passed among you, Mara, mighty among dreamers,
 mighty for ill. He did come upon another who may work with the stuff of dreams
 in a different way. He did meet with Dharma, who may expel a dreamer from his
 dream. They did struggle, and the Lord Mara is no more. Why did they struggle,
 deathgod against illusionist? You say their ways are incomprehensible, being
 the ways of gods. This is not the answer.”
    -Roger Zelazny, “Lord of Light”. 1967.

“He who lives looking for pleasures only,
 his senses uncontrolled, immoderate in his food,
 idle, and weak, Mara will certainly overthrow him,
 as the wind throws down a weak tree.”
    -The Buddha, _Dhammapada_, 1:7.
     trans. F. Max Muller
entries.translation:
“今夜，幻象之主玛拉从你们中间经过，他在梦者中强大，作恶亦强大。他遇见另一位以不同方式操纵梦境者：达摩，能将做梦者驱出梦。他们争斗，玛拉不复存在。死神为何与幻术师争斗？你们说，神的道路无法理解。这不是答案。”
    -Roger Zelazny, “Lord of Light”. 1967.

“只追求享乐、感官不受约束、饮食无度、懒惰虚弱的人，必被魔罗摧倒，如风摧弱树。”
    -The Buddha, _Dhammapada_, 1:7.
     trans. F. Max Muller

entries.english:
“‘Stop thief! Stop thief!’ There is a magic in the sound. The tradesman leaves
 his counter, and the car-man his waggon; the butcher throws down his tray; the
 baker his basket; the milkman his pail; the errand-boy his parcels; the
 school-boy his marbles; the paviour his pickaxe; the child his battledore.
 Away they run, pell-mell, helter-skelter, slap-dash: tearing, yelling,
 screaming, knocking down the passengers as they turn the corners, rousing up
 the dogs, and astonishing the fowls: and streets, squares, and courts, re-echo
 with the sound.”
    -Charles Dickens, _Oliver Twist_. 1838.
entries.translation:
“捉贼！捉贼！”声音有种魔力。商人离开柜台，车夫离开货车；屠夫扔托盘，面包师扔篮子，送奶工扔桶，跑腿童扔包裹，学生扔弹珠，铺路工扔鹤嘴锄，孩子扔球拍。他们乱哄哄飞跑，撕扯、叫喊、尖叫，转角撞倒行人，惊起狗，吓坏鸡；街道、广场和庭院全回荡着这声音。
    -Charles Dickens, _Oliver Twist_. 1838.

entries.english:
“And Heaven came, bringing on night and longing for love, and he lay about Earth
 spreading himself full upon her. Then the son from his ambush stretched forth
 his left hand and in his right took the great long sickle with jagged teeth,
 and swiftly lopped off his own father's members and cast them away to fall
 behind him. And not vainly did they fall from his hand; for all the bloody
 drops that gushed forth Earth received, and as the seasons moved round she bare
 the strong Erinyes and the great Giants with gleaming armour, holding long
 spears in their hands, and the Nymphs whom they call Meliae all over the
 boundless earth.”
    -Hesiod, _Theogony_, 182-187, trans. H.G. Evelyn-White. 1920
entries.translation:
“天带着夜与爱欲到来，覆在地上。儿子从埋伏中伸左手，右手持巨大长锯齿镰，迅速割下父亲生殖器，抛到身后。它们并未徒然坠落：喷出的血滴全由大地承接。时序流转，大地生出强大的复仇女神、披亮甲持长枪的巨人，以及遍布无边大地、名为墨利埃的宁芙。”
    -Hesiod, _Theogony_, 182-187, trans. H.G. Evelyn-White. 1920

entries.english:
“Ye men of Egypt, ye have heard your king!
 I go, and I return not. But the will
 Of the great Gods is plain; and ye must bring
 Ill deeds, ill passions, zealous to fulfil
 Their pleasure, to their feet; and reap their praise,
 The praise of Gods, rich boon! and length of days.”
    -Matthew Arnold, _Mycerinus_
entries.translation:
“埃及人啊，你们已听见王言！
我去，不再回来。但伟大神祇意旨明确：
把恶行恶念带到祂们脚下，
热切满足祂们的喜悦，
收获诸神赞赏——丰厚恩赐——
以及长久岁月。”
    -Matthew Arnold, _Mycerinus_

entries.english:
“Lord, Lord! methought, what pain it was to drown!
 What dreadful noise of waters in mine ears!
 What ugly sights of death within mine eyes!
 Methought I saw a thousand fearful wrecks,
 Ten thousand men that fishes gnawed upon,
 Wedges of gold, great anchors, heaps of pearl,
 Inestimable stones, unvalued jewels,
 All scattered in the bottom of the sea:
 Some lay in dead men’s skulls; and in those holes
 Where eyes did once inhabit, there were crept,
 As ’t were in scorn of eyes, reflecting gems.”
    -William Shakespeare, _King Richard III_, I, iv. 1597
entries.translation:
“主啊，溺水何等痛苦！
耳中可怕的水声，眼里丑恶的死亡！
我仿佛看见千艘骇人沉船，
万具被鱼啃食的人，
金锭、巨锚、珍珠堆，
无价石与宝玉散落海底。
有的躺在死人头骨中，
曾容双眼的孔穴里爬入反光宝石，
仿佛嘲笑眼睛。”
    -William Shakespeare, _King Richard III_, I, iv. 1597

entries.english:
“Then up it raise the mermaiden,
 Wi the comb an glass in her hand:
 ‘Here's a health to you, my merrie young men,
 For you never will see dry land.’”
    -“Sir Patrick Spens”, Scottish folk song, version 58J in Francis James
     Child, _The English and Scottish Popular Ballads_. 1898.
entries.translation:
“美人鱼浮上来，
手拿梳子与镜子：
敬你们一杯，快活年轻人，
你们再也见不到陆地。”
    -“Sir Patrick Spens”, Scottish folk song, version 58J in Francis James
     Child, _The English and Scottish Popular Ballads_. 1898.

entries.english:
“Damn ye! Let Neptune strike ye dead, Winslow! HAAARK! Hark Triton, hark!
 Bellow, bid our father the Sea King rise from the depths full foul in his fury!
 Black waves teeming with salt-foam to smother this young mouth with pungent
 slime, to choke ye, engorging your organs ‘til ye turn blue and bloated with
 bilge and brine and can scream no more -- only when he, crowned in cockle
 shells with slitherin’ tentacled tail and steaming beard take up his fell
 be-finnéd arm, his coral-tine trident screeches banshee-like in the tempest and
 plunges right through yer gullet, bursting ye -- a bulging bladder no more, but
 a blasted bloody film now -- a nothing for the harpies and the souls of dead
 sailors to peck and claw and feed upon, only to be lapped up and swallowed by
 the infinite waters of the dread emperor himself -- forgotten to any man, to
 any time, forgotten to any god or devil, forgotten even to the sea, for any
 stuff or part of Winslow, even any scantling of your soul is Winslow no more,
 but is now itself the sea!”
    -Thomas Wake, _The Lighthouse_. 2019
entries.translation:
“该死的温斯洛！愿海神将你击毙！听啊，特里同，听！咆哮，唤我们的海王父亲从深处愤怒而起！黑浪满载盐沫，以刺鼻黏液堵住你的年轻嘴巴，呛死你，灌满内脏，让你因舱底污水与盐水变得青紫肿胀，再也无法叫喊。直到祂头戴贝壳冠，拖着滑溜触须尾、蒸腾胡须，举起带鳍恶臂，珊瑚尖三叉戟在风暴中如女妖尖叫，贯穿你的咽喉，将你刺爆！不再是鼓胀皮囊，只剩破碎血膜，任鸟妖和亡水手之魂啄抓吞吃，最后被可怕帝王无尽的海水舔食咽下。被所有人、所有时代遗忘，被神和魔遗忘，甚至被海遗忘，因为温斯洛的任何一部分，哪怕一丝灵魂，都不再是温斯洛，而是海本身！”
    -Thomas Wake, _The Lighthouse_. 2019
